title: Relative projective space
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $r\in\mathbb N$. Let $F=\mathcal O_X^{\oplus(r+1)}$ be the sheaf of free $\mathcal O_X$-modules with ordered basis $e_0,\ldots,e_r$, and let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}(F)$ be its symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction], with degree-one sections $T_i=j_F(e_i)$. Use the grading by symmetric degree [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]: the degree-$n$ subsheaf is generated by the monomials $T_0^{a_0}\cdots T_r^{a_r}$ with $\sum_i a_i=n$, and degree zero is $\mathcal O_X$. The constructed pair $(\mathcal A,j_F)$ satisfies the symmetric-algebra universal property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core], so it is canonically isomorphic, preserving $j_F$, to the pair in [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra]. Thus the latter supplies quasi-coherence and the affine-section identification needed for relative Proj; on an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, the standard-basis identification [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] writes this graded algebra as $R[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$ with each $T_i$ of degree one.

Define the scheme over $X$
$$
\mathbf P^r_X=\operatorname{Proj}_X(\mathcal A),\qquad \pi:\mathbf P^r_X\longrightarrow X,
$$
using the construction [def-nagata-relative-proj] and its existence and compatible affine restriction isomorphisms [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]. The standard open $U_i=D_+(T_i)$ is the open specified on each affine base open $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ by $D_+(T_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(R[T_0,\ldots,T_r])$. Its chart identification is the standard affine Proj identification [def-nagata-affine-proj]
$$
U_i\cap\pi^{-1}(V)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\bigl((R[T_0,\ldots,T_r])_{(T_i),0}\bigr),
$$
where degree-zero homogeneous localization has the meaning of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. These chart identifications are those of the relative Proj construction, including their compatibility with restriction on the base; no separate choice of chart isomorphisms is made.

This is the relative-Proj interface, not the base-change definition of [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]; the latter remains the separate interface for downstream results that use only a scheme over the base.
